clauses.text: Support side lengths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16.
Each board is square.
Every face occurs exactly twice.
Number positions from zero in row order.
Reveal the first eligible card.
Reactivating that card has no game effect.
Activating a matched card has no game effect.
Reveal a different unmatched card on the second valid activation.
Keep a matching pair revealed.
Add one matched pair immediately.
Show mismatching faces for 800 active milliseconds.
Close both cards together when that interval ends.
Ignore every card activation during the interval.
Pause the interval while the page is hidden.
Pause the interval while an imported snapshot awaits Resume.
Add one move on the second valid reveal.
The first reveal adds no move.
Ignored activation adds no move.
A match and a miss each cost one move.
Stop increasing the move count at 999999.
Play continues normally at the move cap.
Pairs still match at the move cap.
The game still completes at the move cap.
Show the current move count throughout play as Moves: N.
Give one point per matched pair and no other score.
Show matched pairs against the total throughout play as Pairs: M/T, where M is matched pairs and T is the total.
Complete the game when every pair is matched.
Show final moves in the completion banner.
Show final elapsed time in the completion banner.
Apply the completion motion in V18.
Start elapsed time on the first valid reveal.
Count active milliseconds while the page is shown.
Pause elapsed time while the page is hidden.
Pause elapsed time while an imported snapshot awaits Resume.
Stop elapsed time at completion.
Rendering frequency doesn't change elapsed time.
Use the same active time for the clock and mismatch interval.
Continue a hidden-page mismatch from its remaining time when the page is shown.
Cap elapsed time at 359999999 milliseconds.
Play continues normally at the elapsed-time cap.
The clock shows the capped elapsed time.
Show the clock throughout play as Time: m:ss. Round elapsed seconds down, pad seconds to two digits and let minutes continue past 59. For example, 3600000ms shows Time: 60:00.
Start at 4x4 when there is no supported saved size.
Use a supported saved size on reload.
Remember the last chosen size after reload.
Start a fresh deal on page load.
A successful board-code or snapshot load saves its size as the last chosen size.
A failed load keeps the saved size unchanged.
New Game starts another deal at the current size.
Restart repeats the same deal.
Changing size starts another deal at that size.
Each of these actions clears selection, matches, moves and elapsed time.
New Game and a size change create a fresh seed.
Restart keeps the current board code.
Record only completed games as a best score for their size.
Replace the best only with fewer moves.
Keep the best after reload.
Equal or worse results keep the saved best.
Starting or restarting keeps best scores.
Show the current size's best moves during play and after completion as Best: N.
Show Best: none before a size has a record.
Invalid board codes show an error and keep the game.
Invalid snapshots show an error and keep the game.
Ignore invalid saved preferences.
Continue playing without saving when storage is unavailable.
Starting, restarting, replacing or leaving a game invalidates pending timer updates.
An earlier game or turn's update can't change the current game.
Use a native select named Grid size.
Each option value is its numeric side length.
After a successful board-code or snapshot load, select the loaded board's size in Grid size.
Name the fresh-deal button New Game.
Start a fresh deal at the current size.
Create a fresh seed for the new deal.
Name the repeat-deal button Restart.
Repeat the same deal.
Keep the current board code.
Put reproduction controls inside native details.
Start the details collapsed.
Use the exact summary Reproduce a game.
Name the input Board code.
Limit its text to 32 characters.
Show the current code after a new deal, Restart or successful load.
Keep an edited draft across card actions.
Name the button Load board.
Validate the draft before replacing the game with the deal's starting state.
Name the textarea Snapshot JSON.
Limit it to 65536 characters.
Also apply D10's UTF-8 byte limit in parsing.
Name the button Export snapshot.
Write readable version 1 snapshot JSON into the textarea.
Allow manual selection and copying.
Leave game state and clock unchanged.
Require no Clipboard API.
Round exported elapsedMs down to integer milliseconds.
Round pending mismatch remainingMs up to integer milliseconds, at least 1ms.
Name the button Load snapshot.
Validate the complete draft before replacing the game.
Load unfinished progress paused.
Show Loaded snapshot. Select Resume to continue.
Load completed progress without pausing and show Loaded completed snapshot.
Show Resume only for an imported unfinished paused game.
Resume clears the imported pause.
Continue unfinished loaded progress.
Block every card activation while paused.
Allow board focus movement while paused.
Move focus to the remembered board tab stop before removing Resume.
A completed imported game stays completed without pausing and shows no Resume button.
On invalid input keep the current game.
Keep the invalid draft for correction.
Load board shows Invalid board code.
Load snapshot shows Invalid snapshot.
A completed snapshot shows a static win banner.
Import plays no celebration.
Import doesn't write a best score.
A later win from unfinished imported progress records a local best under R10.
Keep focus on New Game and Restart after activation.
Keep focus on load and export buttons after activation.
These actions don't move focus to the board.
Resume moves focus as required by C10.
Use I12 for the remembered board tab stop after a deal change.
Keep replay in the developer CLI and game core.
Provide no replay controls in the game UI.
npm run --silent replay -- PATH reads replay JSON and prints the final snapshot.
On valid replay input print only the final snapshot JSON to stdout and exit 0.
On invalid replay input print nothing to stdout, a message to stderr and exit nonzero.
Each card is a native button.
Primary click, completed tap, Enter and Space use the same activation action.
Ignore keyboard autorepeat for Enter and Space.
Keep the normal context menu for right-click and long-press.
Opening that menu doesn't activate a card.
Hover leaves game state unchanged.
Pointer cancellation leaves game state unchanged.
Give the board one remembered tab stop.
Tab enters at that card.
Use the first card before any board focus is remembered.
ArrowLeft moves to the previous card in the same row.
ArrowRight moves to the next card in the same row.
ArrowUp moves to the previous row in the same column.
ArrowDown moves to the next row in the same column.
Home moves to the first card in the row.
End moves to the last card in the row.
Ctrl+Home moves to the first card on the board.
Ctrl+End moves to the last card on the board.
Movement changes focus without activating a card.
Arrow movement stops at board edges without wrapping.
Native Tab and Shift+Tab leave the board.
Movement keys navigate without putting every card in the page tab order.
Matched cards stay focusable.
Matched cards have aria-disabled=true.
Matched-card activation follows R02.
Allow focus movement during a mismatch interval.
Block card activation during that interval.
Initial load keeps the browser's current focus.
A new deal or Restart resets the remembered tab stop to the first card.
A successful board or snapshot load resets it to the first card.
Scroll each focused card into view with nearest alignment inside the board.
Give every card a scroll margin of at least 6px so its complete focus outline stays in view, including mid-board cards.
Name hidden cards by one-based row, column and closed state. For example, Row 1, column 1, closed.
Hidden cards keep face SVG out of the DOM.
Hidden cards keep face identifiers out of attributes and accessible text.
Revealed and matched names include position, face name and state.
Use V13's face names.
Use one polite atomic live region.
Announce each turn result exactly once.
Announce a final match and win together once.
Consecutive identical results each have their own announcement.
Focus movement, clock renders and mismatch closing don't repeat a result.
Announce the first match as "Pair found. 1 pair matched." Announce later matches as "Pair found. M pairs matched.", where M is matched pairs.
Announce a miss as No match. Cards close after a short pause.
Announce the final match as "Pair found. All pairs found in N moves and time.", where N is moves and time uses the R07 display format.
Send the load statuses in Controls through the same live region once per load event. Keep the visible status beside reproduction controls.
Support a complete 4x4 keyboard game with a screen reader. Deliver automated accessibility-tree evidence for this journey.
Find Grid size and New Game by name.
Expose closed positions, revealed face names and states and one live-region result per turn in the accessibility tree.
Make the win, final moves and time available.
Tab out of the board and start another game.

Record the browser and tool versions in the project README and whether a screen reader was used. If used, record its name and version. The user confirms spoken output during acceptance. Spoken confirmation is not the developer deliverable.
Use native controls.

Allow both axes to scroll inside the board area.
Keep cards square between 44px and 88px based on available board width.

Use a 2px card border.
Use an 8px card radius.
Fit the four-column board within a phone viewport.
Keep 44px cards and scroll inside the board when a larger board reaches that minimum.
Page background is #090B14.

Positive layout gaps, padding and margins you set use 4px, 6px, 8px, 12px, 16px, 24px or 32px. Allow zero resets and automatic centering. Reset browser default margins. Native control internals are not covered.
Borders, radii, focus, font metrics and SVG coordinates use their own stated values.
Generate 128 distinguishable face identities.
Use integer face IDs from 0 through 127.
Use circle, square, triangle, diamond, star, hexagon, plus and chevron shapes.
Use top, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, left and top-left markers.
Use solid and outline fills.
Shape is id % 8 in the stated shape order.
Marker is floor(id / 8) % 8 in the stated marker order.
Fill is floor(id / 64) with solid then outline.
Color is the palette entry at the marker index.
Shape, marker and fill define identity.
Color repeats the marker distinction without adding an identity.
Use viewBox 0 0 100 100.
Center the main shape within x=25..75 and y=25..75.
Draw the marker above the shape as a radius-5 circle 40 units from the center.
Give the marker a 3-unit Face-background stroke.
Normalize diagonal offsets to about 28.284 units per axis.
Use a 5-unit stroke for outlined shapes.
Distinguish all 128 identities at 44px in grayscale, including solid and outline squares with diagonal markers.
Use the face color for the solid shape's fill, the outlined shape's stroke and the marker's fill. An outlined shape has no fill. The marker keeps its Face-background stroke.
Name faces with lowercase palette, fill, shape and marker names.
Use the form {color} {fill} {shape}, marker {position}.
Use the same neutral-diamond back for every hidden card.

Parse exactly np1-N-seed with a supported side length.
Seed is an integer from 1 through 2147483646.
Use decimal digits without leading zeros.
Trim surrounding whitespace in the Board code control before parsing. The parser accepts only the exact D01 format.
np1 fixes the generation algorithm.
The same code gives the same deck in every supported runtime.
Generation changes need another version.
Time, animation and other random draws can't change the deck.
Initialize Park-Miller state to seed.
Each draw sets state = (state * 16807) % 2147483647 with exact integer arithmetic.
Build paired faces from 0 through N * N / 2 - 1 in ascending order.
Shuffle downward from N * N - 1 through 1 by swapping i with a draw in 0..i.
Use q=2147483646 and limit=floor(q / b) * b for a draw with b results.
Advance the generator and set x=state - 1.
Retry when x >= limit and otherwise return x % b.
Snapshots have exactly version, boardCode, matched, selection, moves, elapsedMs and started.
Snapshot version is 1.
matched contains matched position indices.
Derive deck, pair count and completion from the fields.
Closed selection has only kind=closed.
One-card selection has only kind=one and index.
Mismatch selection has only kind=mismatch, first, second and remainingMs.
Validate the whole snapshot before replacement.
Reject unknown keys.
Require unique in-range matched indices containing whole face pairs.
Selection indices are in range and unmatched.
Mismatch indices are distinct and have different faces.
remainingMs is an integer from 1 through 800.
Completion requires closed selection.
started is boolean.
moves and elapsedMs are nonnegative safe integers.
moves is at least matched pair count plus one for pending mismatch.
Not started requires zero moves and time, no matches and closed selection.
Started with zero moves requires one revealed card.
Import of unfinished progress pauses the clock and mismatch until Resume. Completed imports stay completed without a pause.
Reject elapsedMs above 359999999.
Reject moves above 999999.
Apply the 999999 move cap to saved best scores too.
Replay has exactly version, boardCode, actions and endMs with version 1.
Each action has exactly atMs and index.
Indices are in range.
Times are nonnegative safe integers.
Action times are nondecreasing.
With actions, endMs is at least the final atMs.
Equal-time actions keep array order.
Replay starts from the code's hidden deal.
Advance to each atMs before activating its index then advance to endMs.
Resolve an interval ending exactly at an action time before that action.
Apply game rules to ignored activation.
Cap replayed elapsed time at 359999999 milliseconds. Action times and endMs stay nonnegative safe integers.
The clock starts at first valid activation and replay time omits hidden-page and imported-pause time.
